```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(descriptr)
library(dplyr)
```

## Introduction

In this document, we will introduce you to functions for generating different 
types of plots.

## Data

The `wholesale_customers` data set contains annual spending by 440 wholesale
customers on six product categories, together with the sales channel and region
of each customer. We use the six spending columns for the continuous plots and
`channel` and `region` for the categorical plots.

```{r egdata}
str(wholesale_customers)
```

## Continuous Data

The following functions will create plots for all or subset of continuous 
variables in the data set.

#### Histograms

Annual spending is concentrated at the low end for every product category, with
a long right tail.

```{r hist}
ds_plot_histogram(wholesale_customers)
```

#### Density Plots

```{r density}
ds_plot_density(wholesale_customers)
```

#### Box Plots

```{r box_single}
ds_plot_box_single(wholesale_customers)
```

#### Scatter Plots

The scatter plots show how spending on fresh products, milk and groceries moves
together across customers.

```{r scatter}
ds_plot_scatter(wholesale_customers, fresh, milk, grocery)
```

## Categorical Data

The following functions will create plots for all or subset of categorical 
variables in the data set.

#### Bar Plot

Hotel/restaurant/cafe customers make up the larger share of the sample, and most
customers are in the other region.

```{r bar}
ds_plot_bar(wholesale_customers)
```

#### Stacked Bar Plot

```{r bar_stacked}
ds_plot_bar_stacked(wholesale_customers, channel, region)
```

#### Grouped Bar Plot

```{r bar_grouped}
ds_plot_bar_grouped(wholesale_customers, channel, region)
```

#### Grouped Box Plots

Grouping by channel and region compares the distribution of fresh and milk
spending across customer segments.

```{r box_group}
ds_plot_box_group(wholesale_customers, channel, region, fresh, milk)
```
